turns.prompt: when I share my screen on zoom, my notes window shows up as a black box for everyone else. they cant see my notes at all. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
Your notes app is set to hide itself from screen sharing, so you see the notes and everyone else gets a black box. Nothing in the code needs fixing.

The repo already defaults this off: `isUndetectable` is `false` in `electron/main.ts:242`. But the app saves your last choice, and your saved settings at `~/Library/Application Support/natively/settings.json` have `"isUndetectable": true`. That turns on macOS content protection for every window, which is the black box Zoom shows.

I couldn't change that file myself because my sandbox can't write outside this repo. Either of these fixes it:

1. **In the app:** open Settings and turn the switch from **Undetectable** to **Detectable**. It's the toggle that says "Natively is currently undetectable by screen-sharing." The change applies right away and is saved.
2. **From your terminal**, with the app fully quit:
   ```
   sed -i '' 's/"isUndetectable": true/"isUndetectable": false/' ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json
   ```
   Then reopen the app.

After that, share your screen again and the notes window should show up for everyone. While that mode was on, the app also hid its main window whenever Zoom was running, so if that window kept disappearing during calls, this fixes that too.

The fix never landed. Your saved setting still says `"isUndetectable": true`, and that file hasn't been written since May 27. Neither the in-app switch nor the terminal command reached it, so content protection is still on and Zoom still gets the black box.

I checked the code behind that switch and it's wired correctly: flipping it turns protection off on every window right away and saves the change. So most likely the switch got clicked twice (on, then back on), or it was flipped in a different copy of the app than the one you run in meetings.

My sandbox still can't write to `~/Library`, so here's the surest way to fix it from your terminal:

1. Quit Natively completely (Cmd+Q, or quit it from the menu bar icon). If it's still running when you save the file, it can write `true` back.
2. Run:
   ```
   sed -i '' 's/"isUndetectable": true/"isUndetectable": false/' ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json && cat ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json
   ```
   The printout should now say `"isUndetectable": false`.
3. Reopen the app, open Settings, and make sure the label reads "Natively is currently detectable by screen-sharing."
4. In Zoom, stop sharing and start again. Zoom keeps showing the old black frame for a window until you restart the share.

If it's still a black box after that, tell me two things and I'll dig further: what the printout in step 2 shows, and whether you share your whole screen or just one window. And if "not working properly" means something other than the black box, tell me what you're seeing.

Nothing has changed on your machine since last time. The settings file still says `"isUndetectable": true` and was last saved May 27, so the fix from my last message never got applied. As long as that setting is on, Zoom will show a black box, and nothing on Zoom's side will change that.

I can't flip it for you because my sandbox can't write to `~/Library`. The quickest fix is one command in your own terminal. Quit Natively fully first (Cmd+Q), then run:

```
sed -i '' 's/"isUndetectable": true/"isUndetectable": false/' ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json && cat ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json
```

Paste me what it prints. It should say `false`. Then reopen the app and restart your Zoom share.

If you'd rather not touch the settings file, I can change the code in this repo so the app always starts with screen-share hiding off, whatever was saved. That only helps once you rebuild and reinstall it, though. The `Natively.app` in `/Applications` is a separate build from May 10, so a code change won't affect it on its own. Tell me if you want that.

If you did run the command and still see a problem, say what's happening, like whether it's still a black box or something else. From here the file looks exactly the same as before.
